newsitem.title: SPAIN: Siemens to finalise Amper deal.
newsitem.headline: Siemens to finalise Amper deal.

text.p: German electronics group Siemens will pay 14 billion pesetas to Spain's Amper on December 2 for an 80 percent stake in Amper Elasa and a 10 percent stake in Amper Datos, daily Cinco Dias reported on Thursday.
No one at Siemens Espana, Siemens' Spanish subsidiary, was immediately available for comment.
The original agreement was signed in May and was due to be finalised before September 30.
The Cinco Dias said Siemens had delayed the deal after presenting it to a competition court.
Telecommunications equipment firm Amper told Spain's stock market commission CMNV yesterday that it had approved the sale and it would be completed on Monday, December 2.

The original deal gave Siemens the option to buy the remaining 20 percent of Amper Elasa. If the deal is finalised on Monday, Siemens will have three months to buy this 20 percent for 3.2 billion pesetas.

Amper's statement did not mention a previously agreed joint-venture with Siemens. This venture was to be called Siemens Telecomunicaciones Espana and it was to be held 66 percent by Siemens with Amper holding the remaining 34 percent of the shares.

In May, Siemens said in the original agreement that it wanted to wait for a resolution in a labour conflict in Amper Telematica before finalising the joint-venture. The conflict has since been settled in an out-of-court agreement.
